stdout: # Moss Turn JSON notes into a daily Markdown digest. Moss prints a summary after writing the digest. ## Quick start ```sh node index.mjs ``` Moss reads the included `notes.json` and writes `digest.md` in your current directory. Requires Node.js 20 or later. ## What you get - Notes sharing a topic appear together. - Markdown headings and bullet lists make the digest readable. - Console summaries show each topic and its notes. ## How it works - Moss reads and parses the JSON source. - It groups each note’s `text` by its `topic`. - It writes the Markdown digest and prints summaries. ## Options | Argument | Behavior | | --- | --- | | Source file | Pass a JSON path after `node index.mjs`. If omitted, Moss uses the included `notes.json`. | See the [reference](docs/reference.md) for documentation. ## FAQ and boundaries ### What input does Moss expect? Use a JSON array of objects with `topic` and `text` fields, as shown in `notes.json`. ### Does it run automatically each day? No. Each command invocation creates a digest; the code includes no scheduler or date filtering. ### Will it preserve an existing digest? No. Each run overwrites `digest.md` in the current directory. ## Contributing Test changes from the checkout with `node index.mjs`, then inspect `digest.md` and the console summaries. ## License Moss uses the [MIT License](LICENSE).
